steps.title: A Vessel Awaits
steps.body: Choose a Vessel slot, bind a character, and use the Tavern as your refuge between expeditions.

steps.title: Build, Then Begin Again
steps.body: Every campaign starts at Character Level 1. What the Tavern permanently remembers is separate from run-only levels, equipment, materials, and consumables.

steps.title: The Door Is Always the Start
steps.body: The Campaign Door can be used without the Mantle or Chronicle. Those systems open later through successful Forest progression.

steps.title: Your First Kept Impressions
steps.body: Resolving this starter lesson—by completing it or skipping it—grants exactly two free Kept Impression tokens (3 slots or less) and exactly one free Race Choice token. The chosen race unlocks permanently for the whole account, not for one Vessel slot.

steps.title: Choose a Vessel
steps.body: A Vessel slot permanently binds one character until that slot is deleted. Character Level does not persist between campaigns.

steps.title: Race and Base Class
steps.body: Race and base class are permanent for this Vessel. Choose the identity you want to build around before confirming the binding.

steps.title: Starting Stats
steps.body: Allocate the Vessel's fixed Level-0 starting-stat pool. These points can be redistributed between campaigns; run-earned Stat Points never join this pool.

steps.title: Begin at Level 1
steps.body: Every new campaign begins at Character Level 1. Level, EXP, and run-earned Stat Points reset when that campaign ends.

steps.title: The Main Hall
steps.body: The Main Hall is the Tavern's central hub. Entering a room replaces the current room view until you return to the Main Hall.

steps.title: Services
steps.body: Mara handles quests and the lender, Krass manages Kept Impressions, the Mantle Room manages unlocked subclasses, and the other rooms cover records, training, Vessel setup, and Tavern Adventurers.

steps.title: The Outside Door
steps.body: The Campaign Door never requires the Mantle or Chronicle. A bound Vessel with a legal starting-stat allocation can begin a campaign.

steps.title: Seven Slots
steps.body: Each Vessel has exactly 7 Kept Impression slots. An Impression consumes its printed slot cost.

steps.title: No Duplicates
steps.body: The same Kept Impression cannot be equipped twice on one character. Different Impressions with similar effects may coexist when legal.

steps.title: A Legal Example
steps.body: A 3-slot Impression plus a 2-slot Impression plus another 2-slot Impression uses all 7 slots exactly.

steps.title: Classless Later
steps.body: KI-182 Classless costs 6 slots and leaves one slot. Its deeper rules are introduced only after Classless becomes available.

steps.title: Tavern Adventurers
steps.body: Six Adventurers begin recruited. The remaining residents join after very easy Forest accomplishments.

steps.title: Permanent Recruitment
steps.body: Once recruited, a Tavern Adventurer is account-wide and can accompany any Vessel. They are never permanently lost.

steps.title: Their Own Decisions
steps.body: Tavern Adventurers are AI-controlled according to personality, class, subclass, and combat role. They never use consumables.

steps.title: Choose Up to Three
steps.body: One Otherworlder may deploy with up to three recruited Tavern Adventurers.

steps.title: Roles Matter
steps.body: Supports, protectors, controllers, and damage dealers change how the party survives and who enemies are likely to target.

steps.title: The Tradeoff
steps.body: Adventurers gain full Character EXP, but combat-earned Onyx is reduced to 0.4x, 0.2x, or 0.1x when one, two, or three Adventurers deploy.

steps.title: Level 1 Every Time
steps.body: A campaign snapshots the Vessel at Character Level 1 with its current starting stats, class/subclass state, Kept Impressions, party, equipment setup, and Chronicle allocation.

steps.title: Run-Only Growth
steps.body: Character EXP, levels, level-earned Stat Points, crafted equipment, materials, and consumables are campaign state.

steps.title: Returning Matters
steps.body: A successful return banks carried rewards and may register exactly one eligible brought-home item into that Vessel's lender collection.

steps.title: One Action
steps.body: On a player turn choose exactly one action: Ability, Charge, Guard, or Consumable. After it resolves, only End Turn remains.

steps.title: Energy
steps.body: Every combatant starts at 0 Energy, gains exactly +1 at the start of each own turn, and normally cannot exceed 7. Charge is a separate +1 Energy action.

steps.title: Cooldowns
steps.body: Cooldowns tick at the end of their owner's turn and never tick on the same turn they are newly applied.

steps.title: Defense Order
steps.body: Crit is determined before defense. Dodge resolves before Block or Guard, then other mitigation, then Shields, then HP.

steps.title: Turn Order and Resources
steps.body: The initiative strip shows the persistent ordering. Class, subclass, status, and Kept Impression resources appear only when relevant.

steps.title: Statuses
steps.body: Directly attached effects do not apply on a Dodged hit. Periodic statuses resolve on their own timing and can Crit unless an explicit effect says otherwise.

steps.title: Mandatory Rest Stop
steps.body: Every normal combat victory enters a mandatory Campsite before the Forest advances.

steps.title: Exhaustion
steps.body: The Campsite automatically removes the difficulty's approved number of Exhaustion stacks.

steps.title: Craft and Equip
steps.body: Crafting is Campsite-only. Crafted gear is campaign-only, and equipment can be changed here.

steps.title: Choose Food
steps.body: Consumables stack in inventory, but the normal base limit is one equipped consumable choice and one use per battle. Consumable selection changes at Campsites.

steps.title: Continue
steps.body: Leaving the Campsite advances exactly one Depth and deals the next three unique Forest cards, except at fixed special boundaries.

contextualLessons.name: Trainer Choice
contextualLessons.body: Learn unlocks the Trainer's subclass; Fight gives up learning for this encounter and offers its SoulfireCore on victory. The Trainer can return in another campaign.

contextualLessons.name: Mantle Unlocked
contextualLessons.body: The Mantle Reliquary is now open. Between campaigns, choose an already-unlocked subclass from this Vessel's base-class family.

contextualLessons.name: Chronicle Unlocked
contextualLessons.body: The Chronicle of Paths is now open. Chronicle Progress earned before this moment was retained.

contextualLessons.name: SoulfireCore Found
contextualLessons.body: SoulfireCores are deterministic source-specific crafting materials used for matching SoulFire equipment at Campsites.

contextualLessons.name: Lender Registration
contextualLessons.body: A successful return lets this Vessel register exactly one eligible brought-home item into its permanent lender catalogue.

contextualLessons.name: Subclass Learned
contextualLessons.body: The subclass is unlocked account-wide. It does not replace the active subclass during this campaign; select it later through the Mantle once the Mantle is open.

helpEntries.title: Core Stats
helpEntries.body: STR, DEX, CON, INT, FTH, CHA, and LCK define universal derived effects and each class/subclass uses its approved two-to-four-stat scaling identity. Forest noncombat checks always end with one relevant core stat deciding the chance.

helpEntries.title: HP & Energy
helpEntries.body: Base Maximum HP is 10, plus 2 HP per CON and 3 Max HP for each Character Level after Level 1. Every combatant starts each battle at 0 Energy, naturally gains exactly 1 at the start of each own turn, and normally has a Maximum Energy of 7.

helpEntries.title: Criticals
helpEntries.body: Base damage Crit Chance is 5% and base Critical Damage is 150% total damage. Crit is determined before defensive mitigation, so a Crit never bypasses Dodge, Block, Guard, resistance, damage reduction, or Shields unless explicit text says otherwise. Only one recursive extra critical application is allowed above 100% Crit Chance.

helpEntries.title: Dodge
helpEntries.body: Base Dodge Chance is 5% and normal Dodge Chance is capped at 85%. Dodge resolves before Block. Effects directly attached to a Dodged hit do not apply.

helpEntries.title: Block & Guard
helpEntries.body: Base Block Chance is 5%, normal Block Chance is capped at 85%, and base Blocked Damage Reduction is 40%. Guard is a player action that guarantees Block against incoming hits until the start of that actor's next turn; it is not limited by the normal 85% Block cap.

helpEntries.title: Shields
helpEntries.body: Shields absorb damage after Dodge, Block/Guard, and other mitigation but before HP. Damage exceeding the remaining Shield carries into HP. Multiple internal Shield layers may exist even though combat presentation shows a combined amount.

helpEntries.title: Healing & Lifesteal
helpEntries.body: Healing can Crit. Outgoing Healing modifies healing a character sends; Incoming Healing modifies healing a character receives. Lifesteal uses only actual HP removed, never overkill, and is affected by Incoming Healing.

helpEntries.title: Statuses
helpEntries.body: Ordinary damage-over-time effects tick at the start of the affected actor's turn, cannot be Dodged or Blocked once applied, can Crit by default, and can defeat a combatant before that combatant acts. Stackable timed effects add stacks and refresh duration; non-stack effects refresh without duplicating unless explicit text says otherwise.

helpEntries.title: Class & Subclass Resources
helpEntries.body: Class and subclass resources use their printed generation, spending, caps, and reset rules. Unless explicit text says otherwise, class/subclass combat resources reset to their normal starting state at the beginning of each battle.

helpEntries.title: Kept Impressions
helpEntries.body: A Vessel normally has 7 Kept Impression slots. The same Impression cannot be equipped twice. Temporary KI stacks, counters, stored values, and once-per-combat state reset each battle unless explicit text says otherwise. KI-182 Classless costs 6 slots.

helpEntries.title: Equipment
helpEntries.body: Weapons have no Base Damage and never add hidden damage to abilities; they provide listed attributes/stats and satisfy weapon requirements. Light/Medium/Heavy armor has 0%/5%/10% built-in mitigation, and Heavy Chest armor imposes -2 Initiative. There is no durability.

helpEntries.title: Crafting
helpEntries.body: All non-starter equipment is crafted at Campsites. Normal enemies supply source-specific materials; minibosses, bosses, and Trainers supply their deterministic source-specific SoulfireCores. Crafted equipment is campaign-only.

helpEntries.title: Consumables & Food
helpEntries.body: Most consumables are fantasy foods. Consumables stack in inventory, can only be equipped/changed at Campsites, and the normal base rule permits one equipped consumable choice and one consumable use per battle. Tavern Adventurers and enemies never use consumables.

helpEntries.title: Trainers
helpEntries.body: A Trainer encounter offers Learn or Fight, and the choice is mutually exclusive for that encounter. Learn unlocks that Trainer's subclass account-wide. Fight gives up learning for that encounter and offers the Trainer's guaranteed source-specific SoulfireCore on victory. The Trainer may appear again in a future campaign.

helpEntries.title: Chronicle of Paths
helpEntries.body: The Chronicle is permanent meta progression separated from Character Level. Normal families rank to 30, gain 1 Chronicle Point per rank, and may allocate at most 30 active CP in a 32-node tree. Classless has its separate Rank 0–12 unlock progression. The Chronicle opens after the first successful Forest return; progress earned beforehand is retained.

helpEntries.title: Mantle Reliquary
helpEntries.body: The Mantle lets a Vessel choose an already-unlocked subclass from its own base-class family between campaigns. It never gates the Campaign Door and opens after the first successful Forest return.

helpEntries.title: Tavern Adventurers
helpEntries.body: Up to three recruited Tavern Adventurers may deploy with one Otherworlder. They start each campaign at Level 1, gain full Character EXP while alive, allocate level-up stats automatically, act through personality/class/subclass/role AI, and never use consumables.

helpEntries.title: Mara's Lender
helpEntries.body: There is no permanent equipment inventory. On a successful alive return, a Vessel may register exactly one eligible item brought home from that campaign into its permanent lender catalogue. Before a future campaign, one registered item may be borrowed for free as a run-scoped Legacy copy. Legacy exists only through Mara's Lender and gives that borrowed copy +50% listed stats and Resistances while leaving bespoke passives, granted abilities, and set bonuses unchanged.

helpEntries.title: Onyx & Chronicle Progress
helpEntries.body: Onyx is carried during a campaign. A successful return banks all carried Onyx; defeat banks half with normal final-result rounding. Tavern Adventurers reduce combat-earned Onyx to 0.4x/0.2x/0.1x with one/two/three deployed. Enemy Chronicle Progress is based on raw enemy Onyx at 1/25 before that currency penalty.

helpEntries.title: Defeat, Return & Continue
helpEntries.body: If all real party members reach 0 HP, the campaign ends even if summons survive. Defeat banks half carried Onyx and all earned Chronicle Progress and permits no lender registration. After a region boss and mandatory Campsite, Return safely settles; Continue preserves the exact run and risks its carried equipment and lender opportunity.

helpEntries.title: Initiative
helpEntries.body: Initiative uses a base 1–6 roll plus floor(Level/3), floor(DEX/9), and explicit Initiative bonuses. Ties randomize among tied combatants. Summons act after real combatants in summon order. Initiative does not silently reroll every round.

helpEntries.title: Forest Stat Checks
helpEntries.body: A noncombat check uses d20 + floor(relevant stat/2) + floor(8 × relevant stat / total core stats) + explicit race, Kept Impression, or contextual bonuses against the event DC. The player chooses one living real party member. Natural 20 is Critical Success; natural 1 is a Critical Failure only if the modified total actually fails, so sufficiently specialized characters can reach true 100% success.

helpEntries.title: Forest Expedition
helpEntries.body: The Forest has 30 Depth. Normal steps show exactly 3 persisted unique cards; no event definition repeats within a campaign. The miniboss is fixed at Depth 15 and the boss at Depth 30. Normal combat victory always leads to a mandatory Campsite.
